title: Reject duplicate JSON keys in latent ceiling evidence corpus
finding: Python json.loads applies last-key-wins semantics by default, so a JSON object containing duplicate root or row keys could pass the exact-field parser after one occurrence was silently discarded. That leaves an ambiguous evidence wire representation even though the parsed Mapping looks valid.
primary_claim: The latent-ceiling file loader now refuses duplicate JSON object keys at every nesting level before Corpus.parse or corpus_sha256 calculation. A last-key-wins payload can no longer masquerade as an unambiguous frozen evidence corpus.
gardener_decision: Use the standard-library json object_pairs_hook in the existing loader and one tiny duplicate-key guard. Do not introduce a schema library, parser wrapper hierarchy, migration subsystem, alternate corpus representation, or second validation path.
acceptance: the committed prediction-only corpus remains structurally valid and incomplete
a duplicate root key is refused even when the final duplicate occurrence contains the otherwise valid value
a duplicate nested item key is refused even when the final duplicate occurrence contains the otherwise valid value
existing exact-field, bucket, status, evidence-ref, and duplicate-item-id refusals remain unchanged
no prediction or partial corpus can publish a numeric ceiling
no OwnerApproval, promotion, gate transition, or benchmark superiority claim is created
